title: Critical Thinking
notes: Critical thinking is the habit of examining a claim before accepting it. Name the conclusion, separate evidence from opinion, and ask what would count against the claim.
A short argument has a claim, a reason, and an assumption that links them. In a paragraph, state the claim first, then the reason, then the assumption you are testing.
Evidence is a fact you can point to: a quotation, a figure, or an observation. An inference is the step from that fact to a conclusion, and it should stay no stronger than the evidence allows.
A circular argument repeats the claim as its own reason. A hasty generalisation treats one case as a rule. An appeal to authority is weak when the cited person is not an expert on that question.

Claim: the poem is hopeful because the last line mentions dawn. The evidence is one word. Dawn can signal a new start, but only if the earlier lines agree. One image is not enough when the surrounding lines are bleak.
